import nki.language as nl

@nki.jit
def tensor_transpose2D_kernel_(x, shape2D):
    P, F = x.shape
    F1, F2 = shape2D

    out = nl.ndarray((P, F), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)

    # Copy input data to the tile
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=tile, src=x)

    # Reshape and transpose
    for p in nl.affine_range(P):
        for i in nl.affine_range(F1):
            for j in nl.affine_range(F2):
                out[p, i * F2 + j] = tile[p, i, j]

    return out

def tensor_transpose2D_kernel_(x, shape2D):
    P, F = x.shape

    tile = nl.ndarray((128, 128), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    
    # Copy data from HBM to SBUF tile
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=tile, src=x)
    
    # Reshape and transpose the data in the tile
    # We need to handle the 2D transpose within the tile
    # We'll use a loop to iterate over the partition dimension
    for p in nl.affine_range(P):
        # Extract the current partition row

        # Copy the transposed data back to the output
        nisa.tensor_copy(dst=out[p, 0:F], src=transposed_tile)
    
    return out
